features.description: Capture git state at audit-envelope-write time and persist as a sidecar evidence file per audit pass. The supervisor (or a new helper module `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/git_state.py`, see D011) runs `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` against the plan's repo cwd at the moment audit_writer finalizes the envelope, parses the output into a structured `GitState` dict with five fields — `staged: list[{path, status}]`, `unstaged_modified: list[{path, status}]`, `untracked: list[path]`, `deleted_staged: list[path]`, `deleted_unstaged: list[path]` — and writes it as JSON to `<plan_dir>/evidence/git-state-<iteration>-<role>.json` (one per audit envelope). **Capture is strictly read-only**: only `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` (and optional `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` for repo detection) are allowed; NO `git add`, `git stash`, `git checkout`, `git restore`, `git reset`, or any other state-mutating subcommand. NO file-system writes outside the single sidecar evidence path. NO env-var mutation. The capture function is pure-input (takes a cwd, returns a dict) and the writer is the only side-effect surface (one JSON write per envelope). NO schema bump in this feature: D004 records that promoting `git_state` to `audit.schema.json` v1.4.0 is a separate conventions plan; today this lives as evidence sidecar so we can shape the structure without locking the schema. Zero behavior change for the supervisor: capture is best-effort — if `git status` fails (not a git repo, etc.) the supervisor logs a warning and continues. F002 + F003 are the features that consume this data; F001 just makes the data exist.
steps: Add `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/git_state.py` with `capture(cwd: Path) -> GitState` and `parse_porcelain(raw: str) -> GitState`. `parse_porcelain` is the testable seam.
Define `GitState` as a TypedDict (or dataclass — match existing module style) with the five fields listed above.

Wire capture into `audit_writer.py` (or wherever envelopes are finalized) such that after the envelope JSON is written, `git_state.capture(repo_cwd)` runs and the result is JSON-dumped to `<plan_dir>/evidence/git-state-<iteration>-<role>.json`.
Handle the not-a-git-repo case: `capture()` returns `None` and the writer logs a warning + skips the sidecar write (does NOT raise).

Tests: `test_git_state.py` parametrized over fixture porcelain outputs covering each of the 5 status combinations (staged-add, staged-modify, unstaged-modify, untracked, deleted-staged, deleted-unstaged, mixed). Use a real `tmp_path` git repo for one end-to-end test (creates files, runs `git add`, runs `git status --porcelain`, asserts parse round-trip).
Tests: synthetic supervisor run that finalizes one envelope → verify `git-state-<i>-<role>.json` lands in the plan's evidence dir with the expected schema.
features.acceptance: (1) `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/git_state.py` (D011 path-correction) exists with `capture(cwd)` and `parse_porcelain(raw)`; both are importable. (2) `parse_porcelain` returns a `GitState` mapping with exactly the 5 keys (`staged`, `unstaged_modified`, `untracked`, `deleted_staged`, `deleted_unstaged`); each value is a list (possibly empty); each entry shape matches the spec. (3) Test file `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_git_state.py` covers: per-status parametrized cases (staged add, staged modify, unstaged modify, untracked, deleted-staged, deleted-unstaged), one mixed case, one empty case, and one real-tmp-path round-trip. (4) Audit envelope finalization triggers a sidecar write at `<plan_dir>/evidence/git-state-<iteration>-<role>.json`; verified by a synthetic supervisor test that runs one volley iteration and asserts the file lands with the expected structure. (5) Not-a-git-repo case: `capture()` returns `None`, supervisor logs a warning, no exception propagates. (6) `audit.schema.json` is NOT modified in this feature (D004 documents the deferral). (7) **Read-only proof — three checks, all asserted in `test_git_state.py`**: (7a) source-level — module imports `subprocess` only and the only argv list passed to `subprocess.run` is `['git', 'status', '--porcelain=v1', '-z']` (or the optional `['git', 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel']` for repo detection); auditor confirms by reading the module + grepping for any other `git` argv. (7b) state-snapshot — test takes a `git status --porcelain` snapshot in a real `tmp_path` repo BEFORE calling `capture()`, calls `capture()`, snapshots AFTER, asserts the two snapshots are byte-identical. (7c) filesystem-isolation — test asserts that during `capture()` no files are created/modified outside the single sidecar evidence path (one approach: snapshot `os.listdir` recursively over `tmp_path` before/after capture excluding the known sidecar; assert no diff). (8) All existing orchestrate test modules stay green.

features.description: Pure-function patch-completeness analyzer that consumes a `GitState` capture (from F001), the repo path, and an explicit `touched_files: set[str]` and returns a structured `CompletenessReport` envelope (NOT just a list — the envelope shape is forward-compatible with future schema promotion per D008). Five detection modes. Mode 1 — `test_imports_uncommitted`: a test file imports a Python module whose source file is in `untracked` or `unstaged_modified`. Mode 2 — `source_imports_uncommitted`: a non-test source file imports a module file that is in `untracked` or `unstaged_modified`. Mode 3 — `test_file_untracked`: a test file matching `test_*.py` or `*_test.py` is itself in `untracked` or `unstaged_modified` — pytest discovery would miss it on a fresh clone. Mode 4 — `generated_artifact_staged`: a path in `staged` matches the generated-artifact deny-list (`__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`, `*.pyo`, `.coverage`, `.DS_Store`, `.pytest_cache/`, `node_modules/`, `.tox/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`). The deny-list lives in the module as a frozenset constant with code comments citing why each pattern is on the list. Mode 5 — `unstaged_dirty_state`: any file in `unstaged_modified` is reported as an INFO-severity finding regardless of touched-set membership (F003 promotes to BLOCK when files fall outside `touched_files` AND no `--unrelated-dirty-state-note` was supplied). **Narrowed scope (D005)**: imports are extracted ONLY from files in `touched_files ∪ staged ∪ unstaged_modified` AND only via Python's `ast` module — bash / yaml / markdown / TOML references are NOT detected. Touched-set narrowing keeps the analyzer's read surface bounded; auditor verifies by inspecting the implementation does not walk the entire repo. Output envelope shape (D008): `CompletenessReport(status: 'pass'|'warn'|'fail', findings: list[Finding], files: list[str])` where each `Finding` is `(mode: Literal[...5 modes], files: list[str], reason: str, severity: 'info'|'warn'|'block', recommendation: str)`. `status` is the maximum severity across findings (`block > warn > info`, empty → `pass`). `recommendation` carries the operator-actionable hint (e.g. `Run: git add scripts/x.py` or `Run: git restore --staged scripts/__pycache__/`). The analyzer is pure: no global state, no logging, no print, only file I/O is reading source files for ast parsing.
steps: Add `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/patch_completeness.py` exporting `check(git_state, repo_root, touched_files) -> CompletenessReport`, the five mode detectors as private functions, and the deny-list as `_GENERATED_ARTIFACT_PATTERNS` frozenset with one `# source:` comment per pattern explaining the rationale.

Define the envelope dataclasses (forward-compat with future schema promotion per D008): `CompletenessReport(status, findings, files)` and `Finding(mode, files, reason, severity, recommendation)`. `mode` is a `Literal` over the 5 mode strings; `severity` is a `Literal['info', 'warn', 'block']`; `status` is the maximum severity across findings (`block > warn > info`, empty findings → `'pass'`).

Import extraction uses Python's `ast` module (parse + walk for `Import` and `ImportFrom` nodes) — NOT regex. Resolve relative imports against the file's package; resolve absolute imports against the repo root + standard import paths. Failures to resolve (e.g. third-party modules) are silently ignored (only flag imports that resolve to in-repo files).

**Touched-set narrowing** (D005): the analyzer walks ASTs only for files in `touched_files ∪ {f.path for f in git_state.staged} ∪ {f.path for f in git_state.unstaged_modified}`. The full repo is NOT walked. `touched_files` is supplied by F003's caller (audit envelope evidence_refs + plan affected_paths); F002's tests pass it explicitly.

Test classification: a file is a test file iff its name matches `test_*.py` or `*_test.py` AND it lives under a path containing `/tests/` or `/test/` OR top-level `tests/` OR top-level `test/`. Match the convention already used in `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/`.

Severity assignment: Modes 1-4 default to `severity='block'`. Mode 5 (`unstaged_dirty_state`) defaults to `severity='info'` — F003 owns the promotion to `block` when files fall outside `touched_files` AND no `--unrelated-dirty-state-note` is supplied (so F002 itself never blocks based on the touched-set heuristic; F003 owns that decision).

Recommendation strings are operator-actionable. Examples: Mode 1 → `Run: git add <path>` or `Run: git add -u <path>`; Mode 3 → `Run: git add <test-path>`; Mode 4 → `Run: git restore --staged <path>` + remediation hint to add to .gitignore.

Tests — **failure-mode positive matrix**: parametrized over (a) untracked needed source (Mode 1 + 2 with `untracked` variant), (b) unstaged-modified needed source (Mode 1 + 2 with `unstaged_modified` variant), (c) test-file-untracked (Mode 3, both `untracked` and `unstaged_modified` variants), (d) staged generated/cache artifact (Mode 4 — one fixture per deny-list pattern), (e) unstaged-dirty-state (Mode 5 — fires INFO regardless of touched-set membership).

Tests — **clean / allowed matrix**: (a) generated/cache file present but in `untracked` (operator hasn't staged it, gitignore convention) → no Mode 4 finding; (b) intentionally-untracked evidence/docs file (e.g. local `evidence/scratch-notes.md`) that no test/source imports → no finding; (c) clean-patch case (everything committed, no unstaged) → `status='pass'`, `findings==[]`; (d) third-party / stdlib imports (e.g. `import pytest`, `import json`) from a touched test file → no spurious finding (resolution failure → silent skip); (e) imports from a non-touched non-staged file are NOT analyzed (touched-set narrowing — verified by a fixture that has a malformed-import file outside the touched set; `check()` returns clean).
Tests — **mixed case**: one fixture with all 5 modes firing simultaneously; assert `status='block'` (max severity), `findings` list contains one entry per mode, `files` is the deduplicated union.
Tests — **schema-promotion-readiness**: serialize a `CompletenessReport` to JSON and back; assert round-trip equality. This pins the envelope shape for future schema promotion.
features.acceptance: (1) `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/patch_completeness.py` (D011 path-correction) exists with `check(git_state, repo_root, touched_files)` exported. (2) Module is pure-function: no global state, no logging side-effects, no `print`; only file I/O is reading source files for ast parsing of files in the touched-set ∪ staged ∪ unstaged_modified set (verified by auditor reading the implementation — full-repo walks are forbidden). (3) Output envelope: `CompletenessReport(status, findings, files)` where `status ∈ {'pass', 'warn', 'fail'/'block'}` (use `'fail'` for the user-facing label; severity escalation is `info < warn < block`); each `Finding` carries `(mode, files, reason, severity, recommendation)`. JSON round-trip works (test pins the shape). (4) `_GENERATED_ARTIFACT_PATTERNS` is a frozenset; each pattern carries a `# source:` comment immediately above citing why (mirrors security-baseline F001's pattern-citation discipline). (5) `mode` and `severity` are `Literal` types enforced by the type annotations; auditor verifies by reading the source. (6) **Failure-mode fixture coverage** — `test_patch_completeness.py` includes at minimum: (6a) untracked needed source, (6b) unstaged-modified needed source, (6c) test file untracked, (6d) test file unstaged-modified, (6e) staged generated-artifact (one assertion per deny-list pattern), (6f) unstaged_dirty_state with INFO severity. (7) **Clean / allowed fixture coverage** — at minimum: (7a) generated artifact in `untracked` (not staged) → no Mode 4 finding, (7b) intentionally-untracked evidence/docs (file no test imports) → no finding, (7c) clean-patch case → `status='pass'`, (7d) third-party / stdlib import → no spurious finding, (7e) imports from non-touched non-staged file are NOT analyzed (touched-set narrowing). (8) Mixed-case test asserts `status='fail'` (max severity), unique findings per mode, deduplicated `files` union. (9) Mode 5 (`unstaged_dirty_state`) fires with `severity='info'` regardless of touched-set membership; F002 NEVER promotes Mode 5 to `block` — that is F003's responsibility. (10) All existing orchestrate test modules stay green.

features.description: Wire the F002 analyzer into the supervisor's pre-signoff hook so a non-empty findings list with `severity='block'` refuses `passes:true`. **Failure-severity carve-out (D009)**: the gate fires at signoff/commit-readiness ONLY — `jarvis dispatch --strict-dry-run` runs the gate and surfaces findings in the dry-run report but does NOT exit non-zero, so operators can preview completeness state without triggering a hard block. The block fires only when the supervisor would otherwise flip `passes:true` and write signoff. Implementation: supervisor calls `patch_completeness.check(git_state, repo_root, touched_files)` after audit-envelope finalization and BEFORE writing signoff; `touched_files = {ref.uri for ref in audit_envelope.evidence_refs} ∪ set(plan.affected_paths or [])`. If `report.status == 'fail'`, raise `PatchCompletenessError` with the report rendered as one line per finding (`<mode> | <severity> | <files> | <reason> | <recommendation>`); the error path writes a `breaker:patch_incomplete` gate-pause INBOX entry (matches existing breaker pattern from F006 of the orchestration plan), persists the rendered report to `<plan_dir>/audit/patch-completeness-<iteration>.json`, and the supervisor exits non-zero. Mode 5 promotion: F003 escalates `unstaged_dirty_state` findings from INFO to BLOCK when the file set falls outside `touched_files` AND no `--unrelated-dirty-state-note` was supplied. Operator overrides are CLI flags on `jarvis dispatch`: `--allow-incomplete-patch <reason>` and `--unrelated-dirty-state-note <reason>`. **Both flags require a reason of `len(reason.strip()) >= 8` characters**, validated at TWO layers: (a) CLI argparse validation rejects short reasons with exit code 2 + remediation message; (b) supervisor-level validation re-checks (defense-in-depth — auditor verifies both layers exist). Override paths record `signoff.patch_completeness = {status, findings, files, override_flag, override_reason, unrelated_dirty_state_note?, unrelated_dirty_files?}` so audit history shows the operator chose to ship past the gate. Override flags are plan-locked, not durable (D002).
steps: Add `PatchCompletenessError` to `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/patch_completeness_gate.py (D011 path-correction; the spec text said scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/errors.py but no errors.py module exists — F003's exception lands in the new gate module alongside the enforce() entry point)` (or wherever existing breaker errors live); `__str__` formats one line per finding (`<mode> | <severity> | <files> | <reason> | <recommendation>`).

Wire the check into supervisor pre-signoff: after audit envelope is finalized but before signoff_writer runs, load the git_state sidecar (from F001), compute `touched_files = {ref.uri for ref in audit_envelope.evidence_refs} ∪ set(plan.affected_paths or [])`, and call `patch_completeness.check(git_state, repo_root, touched_files)`. Persist the full report to `<plan_dir>/audit/patch-completeness-<iteration>.json` regardless of outcome (so dry-run and block paths both leave evidence).

Severity promotion (Mode 5): if a Mode 5 finding has any file outside `touched_files` AND `--unrelated-dirty-state-note` is NOT supplied, escalate that finding's severity from `info` to `block` and recompute `report.status`. If the note IS supplied, leave severity at `info` and record the note in the signoff block.

If `report.status == 'fail'` after promotion AND no override flag is supplied: build the gate-pause INBOX entry (event_type=`breaker:patch_incomplete`, payload=report), emit notification via existing notifier hook, raise `PatchCompletenessError`. Supervisor exits non-zero.

**Dry-run carve-out (D009)**: `jarvis dispatch --strict-dry-run` calls `check()` and persists the report + renders the findings in the dry-run output, but does NOT raise `PatchCompletenessError` and does NOT exit non-zero. Verified by an integration test that runs strict-dry-run with deliberate Mode-3 fixture and asserts exit code 0 + findings visible in stdout.

Add CLI flags to `jarvis dispatch`: `--allow-incomplete-patch REASON` and `--unrelated-dirty-state-note REASON`. Both go through CLI argparse validation (layer A): empty/missing reason → argparse error; `len(reason.strip()) < 8` → custom validator action raises `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` with remediation message and CLI exits 2.

Defense-in-depth (layer B): supervisor re-validates `len(reason.strip()) >= 8` when consuming the flag. If validation fails at this layer, raise `ValueError` with the same remediation message — this catches programmatic supervisor invocations that bypass argparse.

When `--allow-incomplete-patch` is set: supervisor records findings + report verbatim AND the override reason in signoff.json under `patch_completeness: {status, findings, files, override_flag: 'allow_incomplete_patch', override_reason: '<verbatim>'}` and proceeds to write signoff (assuming other gates pass).

When `--unrelated-dirty-state-note` is set: supervisor records the note in `patch_completeness.unrelated_dirty_state_note` and the file list in `patch_completeness.unrelated_dirty_files`. Mode 5 finding stays at INFO severity; signoff proceeds.

Update `signoff.schema.json` (or the local validator) to accept the new optional `patch_completeness` block with the schema: `{status, findings: [...], files: [...], override_flag?, override_reason?, unrelated_dirty_state_note?, unrelated_dirty_files?}`. Schema bump to v1.4.0 deferred (D004) — validator-level acceptance only in this feature.
Tests — **block path**: synthetic plan with Mode-3 fixture → supervisor raises `PatchCompletenessError`, signoff NOT written, INBOX entry emitted, `audit/patch-completeness-<i>.json` lands.

Tests — **override path with allow_incomplete_patch**: same fixture + `--allow-incomplete-patch "smoke-test override"` → signoff written, `signoff.patch_completeness.findings` matches the report, `override_reason` is verbatim.
Tests — **unrelated-dirty block**: fixture with unstaged_modified file outside touched_files + no note → Mode 5 escalates to BLOCK, supervisor raises.
Tests — **unrelated-dirty allow with note**: same fixture + `--unrelated-dirty-state-note "WIP on parallel plan X"` → signoff written, note + files recorded under `signoff.patch_completeness`.

Tests — **CLI ≥8-char validation (layer A)**: argparse rejects `--allow-incomplete-patch "wip"` with exit 2; rejects `--unrelated-dirty-state-note ""` with exit 2; remediation message present in stderr.

Tests — **supervisor ≥8-char validation (layer B)**: programmatic supervisor invocation with `reason='wip'` raises `ValueError`; this is a separate test from the CLI test to confirm both layers exist.
Tests — **dry-run carve-out**: `jarvis dispatch --strict-dry-run` with deliberate Mode-3 fixture → exit code 0, findings rendered in dry-run output, no INBOX entry, no PatchCompletenessError raised.

Tests — **clean-patch regression**: existing-plan signoff path with no findings → signoff identical to today's flow, no `patch_completeness` block written (or written with `status='pass'` and empty findings — pick one and pin it in the test).

Tests — **signoff evidence visibility**: assert that when override fires, `signoff.patch_completeness.findings` matches the F002 report exactly (deep equality on findings list); assert `override_flag` matches the flag actually used (`allow_incomplete_patch` or `unrelated_dirty_state_note`).
features.acceptance: (1) `PatchCompletenessError` exists in `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/patch_completeness_gate.py` (D011 path-correction); its `__str__` is multi-line operator-readable with the full per-finding format `<mode> | <severity> | <files> | <reason> | <recommendation>`. (2) Supervisor refuses signoff with a non-zero exit and `breaker:patch_incomplete` INBOX entry when F002 returns `status='fail'` (after Mode 5 promotion) AND no override flag is supplied. (3) `<plan_dir>/audit/patch-completeness-<iteration>.json` lands on every check invocation (dry-run, block, override) — auditor and operator can both inspect the report. (4) **Dry-run carve-out (D009)**: `jarvis dispatch --strict-dry-run` runs the gate, surfaces findings, but does NOT exit non-zero — verified by integration test. The block fires at signoff/commit-readiness only. (5) **CLI ≥8-char validation**: `--allow-incomplete-patch` and `--unrelated-dirty-state-note` both reject `len(reason.strip()) < 8` at the CLI layer with exit code 2 + remediation message; verified by tests parametrized over short reasons (`''`, `'wip'`, `'   '`, `'fix'`). (6) **Supervisor ≥8-char validation**: same length check repeats at supervisor consumption — programmatic invocations raise `ValueError`; verified by a test that bypasses CLI and calls supervisor directly. (7) **Override evidence in signoff.json**: when override fires, `signoff.patch_completeness` contains `{status, findings, files, override_flag, override_reason, unrelated_dirty_state_note?, unrelated_dirty_files?}` — `findings` matches F002's report verbatim (deep equality test), `override_reason` is verbatim CLI input. (8) Mode 5 promotion: unstaged-modified files outside `touched_files` with no note → severity escalates from `info` to `block` and supervisor blocks; with note → severity stays `info`, note + files recorded, signoff proceeds. (9) Both override flags are plan-locked (per-dispatch CLI flags, not durable config) — D002 records this. (10) Test coverage: at minimum 9 distinct tests — block path, allow_incomplete_patch override path, unrelated-dirty block, unrelated-dirty allow-with-note, CLI layer-A short-reason rejection (parametrized), supervisor layer-B short-reason rejection, dry-run carve-out, clean-patch regression, signoff evidence shape. (11) Validator-level acceptance of `patch_completeness` block in signoff.json (no schema bump in this feature; v1.4.0 promotion deferred per D004). (12) All existing orchestrate test modules stay green.
